newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Moody's may up ratings of 11 Philippine banks.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may up ratings of 11 Philippine banks.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service placed under review for possible upgrade the long-term foreign currency debt and deposit ratings of eleven Philippine banks.

The rating review follows Moody's announcement that it was placing on review for possible upgrade the Ba2 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds and notes of the Republic of the Philippines, as well as the country's Ba3 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bank deposits.
The banks' short-term ratings of Not-Prime are confirmed as are their individual Bank Financial Strength Ratings (BFSR).
The eleven banks on review for possible upgrade are:
1. Allied Banking Corporation : Ba2 (senior long-term debt); Ba3 (long- term bank deposits)
2. Bank of the Philippine Islands:Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
3. Development Bank of the Philippines:Ba2 (senior long-term debt); Ba3 (long- term bank deposits)
4. Equitable Banking Corporation:Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
5. Far East Bank and Trust Co. :Ba2 (senior long-term debt); Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
6. Land Bank of the Philippines:Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
7. Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co MBT.PS : Ba2 (senior long-term debt); Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
8. Philippine Commercial International Bank: Ba2 (senior long-term debt); Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
9. Philippine National Bank :Ba2 (senior long-term debt); Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
10. Rizal Commercial Bank Corp : Ba3 (long-term bank deposits)
11. United Coconut Planters Bank: Ba2 (senior long-term debt); Ba3 (long-term bank deposits).

Moody's said that the banks' foreign-currency ratings are constrained by the Ba2 sovereign ceiling of the Republic of the Philippines for foreign currency bond obligations and Ba3 sovereign ceiling of the Philippines for foreign currency deposits.
Moody's said that the rating differential between the country's bond and deposit obligations reflects the implied subordination of deposits to bonds in a stress scenario.

The rating agency said that the review of the Ba2 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds and notes of the Republic of the Philippines was prompted by the successful macro-economic policies implemented in recent years, in particular the substantial effort made in fiscal adjustment.

The government's commitment to strengthening its fiscal accounts has been reflected in its pursuit and implementation of important tax measures, including an expanded value-added-tax and the crucial excise tax passed last November.

This will bolster its revenue base and reduce its dependence on one-off privatization receipts. Structural reforms have improved the economy's international competitiveness, encouraged increased foreign investor interest, reduced inflation, and triggered a robust export performance.

Additionally, the external foreign currency debt burden has moderated. As part of the review process, Moody's will focus on both the political and economic factors affecting the sustainability of these favorable developments over the medium-term.
